interpretations.text: The finite-budget native search found a lower but still failing signed maximum excess: J decreased from 20.426785753066465 to 11.816439876751495, an exact reduction of 8.61034587631497 in normalized units. The baseline worst constraint was holding speed, 0.4285357150613293 m/s against a 0.02 m/s limit at 0.45 s. In the best sampled result, the worst constraint changed to holding position error: 0.12816439876751495 m against a 0.01 m limit at 0.45 s, yielding normalized signed excess 11.816439876751495. Thus the best found sequence remains a valid evaluated task failure within the sampled native-model scope.

The search substantially reduced holding speed to 0.2536984073471587 m/s from 0.4285357150613293 m/s, a decrease of 0.1748373077141706 m/s. However, holding position error increased from 0.12402622706010982 m to 0.12816439876751495 m, an increase of 0.00413817170740513 m; terminal error was also 0.1264496051238062 m in the best result. This trade-off weakens any explanation that the searched control sequence uniformly improved task behavior. Because the comparison changes many control coefficients jointly, it does not identify a causal coefficient, physical failure mechanism, or structural limitation.

Global capability and task acceptance remain unresolved. The 24-dimensional search stopped at its evaluation-request budget after 120 optimization evaluations, 120 rollouts, and 120000 native physics steps; convergence and global optimality were not established. The evidence covers sampled native-model checks over 0–0.5 s under the frozen initialization and ideal bounded tendon tensions of 0–8 N, but independent task acceptance is unmeasured. Consequently, failure of this finite search does not prove global nonlinear infeasibility, structural infeasibility, hardware failure, robustness, or repeatability. A full independent 0-to-duration replay and applicable frozen acceptance evidence are missing and would discriminate a model-search failure from an accepted physical-task result.

The registered execution was a valid but failed physical-task evaluation. Terminal position error was 0.1264496051238062 m against a 0.01 m limit, an excess of 0.1164496051238062 m. Holding maximum position error was 0.12816439876751495 m against 0.01 m, an excess of 0.11816439876751495 m and the dominant normalized constraint gap (11.816439876751495). Holding maximum speed was 0.2536984073471587 m/s against 0.02 m/s, an excess of 0.2336984073471587 m/s. Force-bound violation was exactly 0.0 N and solver-error count was exactly 0, so those two constraints passed. These results establish failure of this execution, not global or structural infeasibility.

Persistent motion during the holding interval is supported as an immediate description of the holding failure. At 0.45 s, tip speed reached the reported holding maximum of 0.2536984073471587 m/s, with velocity [0.0822753779226852, -0.10703684124359165, 0.21479468963351572] m/s. At 0.50 s, speed remained 0.18958003507412524 m/s—still far above the 0.02 m/s holding limit—and the velocity changed to [-0.05632481680159382, -0.00602278801184894, -0.1809194039774003] m/s. The directional reversals are consistent with ongoing transient or oscillatory motion rather than settled holding. However, this does not identify its cause: force limits were respected, and no controller diagnostics or diagnostic relations are available to distinguish inadequate damping, tracking, actuation allocation, or another mechanism.

The evidence cannot determine why the system remained far from the target and continued moving. Position error at the two critical samples is unavailable, recorded control diagnostics are unavailable, and zero solver errors only excludes recorded solver failure—not dynamic, modeling, or control deficiencies. A discriminating assessment would require synchronized target and position-error trajectories, commanded versus actual tendon tensions, controller state/output diagnostics, and the complete holding-window time series. Repeat executions would also be required to assess repeatability or robustness; the present record contains one physical launch and cannot support hardware-performance, continuous-time-compliance, or global-feasibility conclusions.

decision.selected_method: legal mixed structure-control search with full control reoptimization after each structural proposal

original_plan.expected_observation: A legal mixed search starts a real Worker and finds at least one structurally modified candidate whose freshly reoptimized bounded control lowers normalized maximum constraint excess relative to 11.816439876751495, ideally producing terminal error and holding-position error at or below 0.01 m and holding speed at or below 0.02 m/s in independent full-task evaluation.
original_plan.fixed_conditions: Keep the frozen target [0.29, -0.035, 0.19] m, 0.5 s horizon, 0.01 s control and sample periods, 0.0005 s integration timestep, all original input bounds, sources, fidelity, initialization, termination conditions, and independent evaluation contracts unchanged; reoptimize control after every structure change and compare only evidence at its registered scope.
original_plan.hypothesis: The current failure is not evidence of structural infeasibility: an authorized mixed change in geometry, routing, or segment parameters, followed by fresh full-horizon bounded control optimization for that changed structure, can substantially reduce the dominant holding-position excess while also settling holding speed and terminal error under all frozen M3 constraints.
original_plan.interpretation: The saved control-only search reduced its objective but remained far from all three reach/hold thresholds, with a speed-position trade-off and no solver or force-bound failure. This motivates a mixed structural search with control adaptation, while preserving the distinction between finite-search failure and structural infeasibility.
original_plan.stopping_condition: Stop this diagnostic stage when the candidate-bound scientific question is admitted and the chosen legal mixed structure-control search is ready to launch; do not treat a finite unsuccessful search as proof of infeasibility.
original_plan.weakening_observation: After fair fresh control optimization for each legal structural proposal, no evaluated proposal improves normalized maximum constraint excess over 11.816439876751495, or improvements in position consistently worsen holding speed or terminal error enough that the maximum excess does not decrease.
